clue.text: His readers found guidance along the right lines

definitions.text: His readers found guidance along the right lines

parts.words: His readers found guidance along the right lines
parts.note: the readers of a Victorian railway timetable found their way along the correct railway lines, named after its compiler

explanation.surface: A mentor whose followers were led in the proper direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right lines' suggests moral guidance, but the lines are railway lines: George Bradshaw published the famous British railway timetables of the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway guide was named after its publisher, George Bradshaw, so its readers were his readers.

clue.text: Gasbags sagging in the mid W I die

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Gasbags sagging in the mid W I die': 'mid W I die' is OCR garble; LIMP (sagging) appears to sit inside B...S but no clue words for B and S survive, and no scan is available
annotationWithheld.clue: Gasbags sagging in the mid W I die

clue.text: Turns aside disposition to 'starve

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement of parts, so the letters of the word that follows are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a natural tendency towards going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' reads as temperament, but here it means arranging: rearrange STARVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to turn it away or deflect it, as one averts one's eyes.

clue.text: Matches 25 years old celebrations

parts.note: matches are marriages, and the parties marking a marriage that has lasted a quarter of a century are the anniversaries meant

explanation.surface: Sporting fixtures held to mark a quarter-century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' suggests games, but here it means marriages; a 25th anniversary is traditionally the silver one.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries of marriage carry traditional materials, and a quarter-century of marriage is marked with silver.

clue.text: A girl beats baffled literate mathematician

indicators.note: baffled means confused, so the letters of the three words before it are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A girl outdoes a well-read but puzzled maths expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literate' looks like a description of the person, but it belongs to the definition: this mathematician works with letters standing for numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra uses letters as symbols for numbers, so a specialist in it is a mathematician working with letters.

clue.text: Sweet nonsense

explanation.surface: A sugary confection that is pure drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: A striped boiled mint is a British sweet, and the same word means deceptive talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Inwardly subdued exorbitant money-lenders whose claims are unjustified

indicators.note: inwardly says the next piece goes inside the moneylenders that follow it

parts.note: usurers are those who lend money at extortionate interest
subdued means quiet, and P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for softly

explanation.surface: Greedy lenders, privately cowed, who have no right to what they demand.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano, softly in music) goes inside USURERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes a throne or position without right holds a claim that cannot be justified.

clue.text: During the journey, incidentally

explanation.surface: Something mentioned in passing while on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means on the road; as an idiom it introduces a passing remark.

clue.text: Under-estimate the person in question? Indentification needed

definitions.text: Under-estimate the person in question? Indentification needed

parts.words: Under-estimate the person in question? Indentification needed
parts.note: a challenge to guess the identity of someone, phrased as estimating the person being asked about

explanation.surface: A warning not to misjudge someone, with ID required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under-estimate' suggests misjudging, but read it as a direction to estimate which person is meant: the phrase used when inviting someone to guess an identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a teasing challenge to name somebody, and is also a children's identification game.

clue.text: Ie goodly version of characteristic thinking

indicators.note: a version of something is a new rendering, so the letters before it are recast in another order

explanation.surface: A pleasant rendition of someone's typical outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IEGOODLY (from 'Ie goodly', i.e. 'that is' plus 'goodly'), which the newspaper scan has as 'Le goodly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of ideas typical of a group or person is their creed or world view.

clue.text: The Victorian lady put such activity behind her

definitions.text: The Victorian lady put such activity behind her

parts.words: The Victorian lady put such activity behind her
parts.note: a padded frame worn at the back of a Victorian dress shares its name with busy activity

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century woman gave up a life of commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put behind her' suggests leaving the past behind, but the frame was literally worn behind, under the skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means energetic activity and also the pad worn under the back of a Victorian skirt.

clue.text: Fuss over British Standard found in a stew

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece over another means it comes first, before the next piece

parts.note: a pother is a commotion or fuss
BS is the abbreviation for British Standard

explanation.surface: A row about a quality standard ends up in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a stew' suggests being flustered, but here it is literal: herbs that go in a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafy plants such as parsley that are boiled in the cooking pot are the ones meant by stew ingredients.

clue.text: Disturbances for the higher echelons?

parts.note: disturbances are upheavals, and sets that are up are the higher levels of society

explanation.surface: Trouble brewing among those at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word as UP SETS: groups higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbances or upheavals are also the word for sets positioned up high.

clue.text: Strange and smooth; it's a v paradoxical game!

parts.note: odd means strange
even means level or smooth

explanation.surface: A game that is both weird and level, which seems a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is paradoxical because its name pairs opposites: odd numbers and even numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A guessing game where players bet on whether a count of items is a number divisible by two or not.

clue.text: Comparatively hairless race? Nonsense!

parts.note: balder means more bald, having less hair
a dash is a sprint or race

explanation.surface: A mocking remark about a contest between bald men.
explanation.walkthrough: BALDER (more bald) + DASH (a sprint).
explanation.definitionFit: Senseless talk or writing is drivel or rubbish.

clue.text: To stimulate promises to pay isn't genuine

parts.note: to spur is to urge on or stimulate
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Encouraging people with debts is a false move.
explanation.walkthrough: SPUR (urge on) + IOUS (promissory notes).
explanation.definitionFit: Something false or counterfeit lacks authenticity.

clue.text: Is the haberdasher keeping or selling it?

definitions.text: Is the haberdasher keeping or selling it?

parts.words: Is the haberdasher keeping or selling it?
parts.note: a draper keeps goods in store, and also sells hosiery, so the same word covers both

explanation.surface: A question about whether a draper is holding on to goods or selling them.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means keeping goods in store and also names a garment a haberdasher would sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding goods in store for sale is the verb sense; a knitted leg covering is the noun sense.

clue.text: See 3
The Wedgwood Arms, in Hertfordshire

parts.note: Josiah Wedgwood was a potter, and a pub named 'Arms' would be his bar, giving a town name

explanation.surface: A pub named after the famous pottery family, located in a Home County.
explanation.walkthrough: A pub called 'The Wedgwood Arms' would be the potter's bar; Potters Bar is a town in Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hertfordshire town's name reads as the pub of a maker of ceramics, which Wedgwood was.

clue.text: Boring 14, but it may bring down the house

definitions.text: it may bring down the house

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
the answer to 14 across means nonsense, and rot is another word for nonsense

explanation.surface: Tedious drivel that nonetheless brings the audience to its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring down the house' suggests a hit show, but here a timber-eating fungus literally makes a house collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal decay of timber can weaken a building until it falls.

clue.text: Old boy, behind time, gets T flattened north and south

indicators.note: behind time means late, and the phrase follows the old boy so its piece comes after

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
behind time means late, so the time piece is late

explanation.surface: A former pupil who is running late gets knocked flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'T' before 'flattened' is a stray mark in the print. 'Flattened north and south' describes a sphere squashed at the poles, as the Earth is.
explanation.definitionFit: A spheroid squashed at its poles, like the Earth, is described this way in geometry.

clue.text: For her, accommodation of W R the best aboard ship

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'For her, accommodation of W R the best aboard ship': 'W R' is OCR garble; BERTH + A is likely but the words supplying A cannot be read with confidence and no scan is available
annotationWithheld.clue: For her, accommodation of W R the best aboard ship

clue.text: Give up again and retire

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to cede is to give up or yield

explanation.surface: Someone surrenders a second time and withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as two definitions, but 'Give up again' is wordplay for the whole word, with 'again' as the prefix placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw or move back, like a tide going out.

clue.text: Lovable incompetent Dora

indicators.note: the word 'incompetent' splits into 'in' plus 'competent', telling us Dora goes inside

parts.note: competent means able
taken as the name written

explanation.surface: A sweet but useless woman named Dora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incompetent' reads as one word meaning useless, but split it as 'in competent': the name sits inside the word for competent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming or endearing inspires affection.

clue.text: Face the East; that is in alternative New Testament initially

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for that is goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the two preceding words

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Turning towards Jerusalem, as in a different version of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies to both words of 'New Testament', taking the first letter of each; 'in' then places the abbreviation for 'that is' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To align oneself towards the sunrise, originally in placing churches, is the verb's root sense.

clue.text: Cloudy advice for the seamstress

explanation.surface: Grey skies prompting a tip for someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky is grey and covered; split as an instruction, it tells a dressmaker to stitch over a raw edge.

clue.text: Stages variety; most wise

indicators.note: variety means diversity of form, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Variety theatre puts on shows; the wisest are involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety' looks like a type of theatre beside 'Stages', but it signals rearranging STAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sage, meaning wise.

clue.text: Put them among three articles as object of hatred

indicators.note: among says the word them is placed within the articles

parts.note: the indefinite articles an, a and a

explanation.surface: An instruction to sort people between three items, of something detested.
explanation.walkthrough: THEM sits among AN, A, A: AN + A + THEM + A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or detested; originally a thing cursed by the church.
